svg.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: SPI timing of one register frame
svg.desc: SPI timing of an ADS9324 register frame in mode 0: CS low frames 24 clocks, SDI carries the 8-bit address and the 16-bit value on the rising SCLK edges and SDOUT shifts out the value asked for, with the setup, hold and delay times of the datasheet.
svg.text: SPI timing of one register frame
SPI mode 0 (CPOL 0, CPHA 0). Datasheet: 5.6 Timing Requirements, p. 11;
5.7 Switching Characteristics, p. 12; 7.5.1 Register Write Operation, Figure
7-41, p. 50; 7.5.2 Register Read Operation, Table 7-17, p. 51.
Setup time from CS falling to the first SCLK capture edge
SCLK high time, as a fraction of tSCLK
SCLK low time, as a fraction of tSCLK
Setup time of SDI before the SCLK rising edge
Hold time of SDI after the SCLK rising edge
Hold time from the last SCLK falling edge to CS rising
CS high time between two frames
Delay from CS falling to data valid on SDOUT
Delay from the SCLK launch edge to the next bit valid on SDOUT
Time the previous SDOUT bit stays valid after the SCLK launch edge
Delay from CS rising to SDOUT high impedance
The datasheet names no SPI mode and calls the SDOUT edge the launch
edge; the driver takes the falling SCLK edge as the launch edge, as
drawn. SDOUT drives the value read for 16 clocks and zeros for the last
8 (Table 7-17). The SDOUT times of 5.7 are given at IOVDD = 1.7 V to 1.9
